idea: Laundry pickup and drop for students in my university hostels

strategist.problem: A hostel student at an Indian university runs out of clean clothes on a Sunday night before a Monday 9am class, and the dhobi or laundry shop near campus is shut, cash-only, or 3 days away — the pain hits the moment they open the wardrobe and have nothing wearable for the week ahead.
strategist.target_customer: Hostel-resident undergraduate students at a single Indian university campus, spending ₹500-₹2,000 a month on food and convenience, who already ask batchmates on WhatsApp for laundry help and will pay to skip the queue and the walk.
strategist.mission: We pick up, wash and return hostel students' laundry on a fixed weekly slot so they never face a Monday with no clean clothes.

competitors.name: Local dhobi and laundry shops near campus
competitors.differentiator: We offer a fixed pickup/drop time slot booked on WhatsApp with UPI payment and per-kg price visibility, while they are walk-in, cash-only and give 2-3 day turnaround.

competitors.name: Hostel dhobi/washing-area service run by mess or wardens
competitors.differentiator: We give a tracked slot with a pickup confirmation message and a fixed return deadline, while theirs is informal, first-come-first-served and unreliable during exam weeks.

competitors.name: Washing machines in hostel common area
competitors.differentiator: We save the 60-90 minute round trip of washing, drying and folding for ₹X per kg, targeting students who value time over the near-zero machine cost.

scope_cuts: No custom mobile app or web dashboard in v1 — the entire booking, pickup confirmation and payment flow runs on WhatsApp plus a Razorpay payment link, because a solo student founder cannot maintain two codebases on 15 hours a week.

No in-house washing infrastructure — we do not buy machines or rent a shop in the first 6 weeks; we subcontract the actual wash to an existing local laundry partner and own only the pickup, tracking and customer relationship.

No delivery beyond one hostel block or one campus — we deliberately serve only 1-2 hostel buildings initially so the pickup route fits in one evening trip, and expand only after 20 paying repeat customers in that zone.

stack.name: WhatsApp Business
stack.why: Primary channel for booking, pickup confirmation, and customer communication within the hostel WhatsApp groups.

stack.name: Razorpay
stack.why: Generates UPI payment links for per-kg or monthly plan billing without building a custom checkout.

stack.name: Google Sheets
stack.why: Tracks daily pickup lists, kg weights, and payment status for the single hostel block.

stack.name: Canva
stack.why: Creates digital posters for hostel notice boards and Instagram reels to announce the weekly slot.

stack.name: Google Business Profile
stack.why: Free local listing for 'Laundry Pickup [University Name]' to capture search traffic from students.

ai_tools.name: Claude
ai_tools.why: Drafts WhatsApp broadcast messages, calculates per-kg pricing based on partner costs, and writes the SOP for the laundry partner.

ai_tools.name: Gemini
ai_tools.why: Free for Indian university students; generates image prompts for Canva posters and summarizes student feedback from text messages.

mvp_features: Weekly fixed-slot laundry pickup and drop for 1 hostel block, billed at ₹40/kg via UPI link.
WhatsApp-based booking with automatic pickup confirmation and return deadline tracking.
Monthly subscription plan at ₹1,200/month covering up to 30kg of laundry with priority handling.

tool_costs.price_note: 2% + GST per payment, no setup fee or AMC. Price checked 2026-11-02 on https://razorpay.com/pricing/

first_10_steps: Visit 3 local laundry shops near campus and record their per-kg wash prices and turnaround times in a Google Sheet.
Create a WhatsApp Business account and set up a catalogue with two items: 'Per-kg Laundry (₹40/kg)' and 'Monthly Plan (₹1,200/month)'.
Generate 3 UPI payment links in Razorpay for ₹40, ₹100, and ₹1,200, and test them with a batchmate.
Design a 1-page Canva poster listing the weekly pickup slot (e.g., Sunday 6 PM) and the UPI link, then print 20 copies for hostel notice boards.
Post the Canva poster and a 30-second voice note in 5 hostel WhatsApp groups, asking for 10 pilot customers for a 50% discount on their first week.
Collect the first 10 pilot bookings via WhatsApp, weigh the laundry at pickup, and send the exact kg-based invoice via Razorpay link.
Subcontract the wash to the cheapest local laundry partner, track the handoff time, and ensure return within 48 hours.
Use Claude to draft a 'Thank You' message with a 10% discount code for the next week, and send it to all 10 pilot customers.
Track the 10 pilot customers in Google Sheets, noting their kg usage, payment method, and feedback on turnaround time.
After 2 weeks, convert 5 pilot customers to the ₹1,200/month plan by offering a free extra 5kg if they commit to a 1-month subscription.

pricing.name: Pilot First Week
features: 50% off first per-kg order for pilot customers
One-time offer for the first 10 bookings

burn_line_items.item: Marketing budget (20 printed posters + 2 reels + ₹500 UPI cashback for referrals)

revenue_targets.notes: 5 pilot customers at 50% discount, blended avg ₹700 (mix of per-kg and one ₹1,200 plan)
Convert 3 pilots to ₹1,200/month plan, add 5 new per-kg customers from WhatsApp groups
5 monthly plans + 10 per-kg regulars in one hostel block; break-even crossed

key_assumptions: One paying customer averages ₹700/month: assumes 40% of customers are on the ₹1,200 monthly plan and 60% buy ~12 kg/month at ₹40/kg (₹480), blended = 0.4×1200 + 0.6×480 = 768, rounded down to 700 to account for the 50% first-week pilot discount in month 1.

Delivery cost of ₹310/customer/month = subcontract wash at ₹25/kg × 12 kg average = ₹300, plus ₹10 packaging/UPI fee; this rate must be confirmed before Day 7 by negotiating with 3 local laundry shops and running a real 5kg sample order to verify both the per-kg rate and 48-hour turnaround — if the confirmed rate is ₹30/kg, delivery cost rises to ₹370 and break-even moves to 8 customers.
Willingness-to-pay assumption: hostel students already spending ₹500-₹2,000/month on convenience will pay ₹40/kg (≈₹160/week for 4 kg) to skip the 60-90 minute wash cycle and the 3-day dhobi wait.
Marketing budget of ₹3,500/month covers 20 printed posters (₹500), 2 Instagram reels with Canva (₹0), and ₹3,000 reserved for first-week 50% discounts absorbed as revenue loss, not burn.

channels.name: Hostel & class WhatsApp groups (one hostel block)
channels.tactic: Join the 6-8 WhatsApp groups of one target hostel block (block group, floor groups, batch groups). Post the ₹20 first-wash offer once per group on Thursday, then send 15 direct messages per day Fri-Sat to members who recently asked for laundry help in those groups; convert to a Sunday 6 PM pickup slot booking. Target: 5 paying customers by Day 30.

channels.name: Instagram Reels + hostel notice-board posters
channels.tactic: Line-item spend: (a) 50 A5 posters printed at ₹8 each = ₹400, pasted Day 1 and re-pasted Day 15 in the target hostel block notice board, stairwell, washroom; (b) ₹1,100 referral cashback pool paid as ₹100 UPI credit to a customer whose forwarded message books a new payer (up to 11 redemptions); (c) ₹2,000 Instagram paid boost = ₹50/day for 40 days on the best-performing Reel, geotagged to the campus. Free layer: 1 Canva Reel/day (bag → weigh → UPI link → folded return) for 30 days. Target: 3 paying customers by Day 30.

first_10_customers: Day 1-2: Walk the target hostel block and paste 50 printed A5 posters (₹8 each, ₹400 total) at the notice board, stairwell, and washroom; note the WhatsApp group names and join 6-8 of them.

Day 3-4: In each joined WhatsApp group, post once: 'Sunday 6 PM pickup from Block __. First wash at ₹20/kg (50% off), returned folded in 48 hours. Reply kg to book.' Then DM 15 members/day who have previously asked for laundry help in the group.
Day 5-6: Lock 5 pilot bookings for the Sunday 6 PM slot; confirm each with a pickup time message and send the Razorpay payment link the moment the bag is weighed.
Day 7-8: Post Reel #1 on Instagram (bag → weigh → UPI link → folded return) with campus geotag; reply to every comment and story mention with the ₹20 offer link.

Day 9-12: Ask each of the 5 pilot customers after return: 'If your roommate or floor-mate also needs this, forward this message — you both get ₹100 off next pickup.' Track forwards manually in a notes sheet and pay ₹100 UPI credit per booked referral from the ₹1,100 pool.

Day 13-14: Convert the 2 most repeat pilot users to a ₹1,200/month plan by DM, and post the group message a second time in the 3 groups that gave the most replies; start the ₹50/day Instagram boost on the top Reel.
growth.cold_message: Hi — I run a Sunday 6 PM laundry pickup from Block __, washed and returned folded in 48 hours, ₹40/kg paid by UPI link after pickup. First wash is ₹20/kg (50% off) for the first 10 bookings this month. Reply with the kg you need and I'll book your slot for this Sunday.

objections.objection: The hostel washing machine / dhobi is cheaper, why should I pay ₹40/kg?
objections.response: You're right — the machine costs almost nothing. You're paying for the 60-90 minutes of washing, drying and folding plus the fixed Sunday 6 PM pickup from your block and a 48-hour return deadline, confirmed on WhatsApp. Try it once at ₹20/kg and decide if your Sunday evening is worth it.

objections.objection: What if you take my clothes and don't return them, or return them late before Monday class?
objections.response: No prepayment — you pay by UPI link only after the bag is weighed at pickup, and every booking gets a WhatsApp confirmation with the exact return deadline. If the return misses the confirmed deadline, that pickup is free. First 10 bookings this month are at ₹20/kg so you can test it with low risk.

critic.verdict: This is a well-scoped, constraint-honoring plan: a WhatsApp + Razorpay laundry pickup service for one hostel block, subcontracting the wash, bootstrapped with ₹15k and zero tool costs until revenue. The pricing, channels and 6-week first-customer timeline are realistic for a campus service, and the scope cuts (no app, no machines, one block) correctly protect a 15-hour-a-week student founder. The main gaps are operational rather than strategic — the plan under-specifies how laundry is actually weighed, handed off and tracked reliably.
critic.biggest_risk: The entire business hinges on a subcontracted local laundry partner delivering ₹25/kg at 48-hour turnaround; if that rate or reliability isn't locked in with a real sample order before Day 7, margins collapse or returns slip before Monday and the WhatsApp group turns hostile.
